title: useSelector
description: Learn how to read data from the Redux store.

data.text: **useSelector** is your primary tool for reading data from the Redux store. It subscribes to the store and automatically updates your component whenever the selected data changes. Think of it as a query for your state.

When you call `useSelector`, you pass a function that receives the entire Redux state and returns the piece you need. The hook subscribes to store updates and triggers a re-render only when the selected value changes.

data.caption: useSelector Subscription Flow
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Component
    participant useSelector
    participant Store
    participant Reducer
    Component->>useSelector: useSelector(selector)
    useSelector->>Store: Subscribe to store
    Store-->>useSelector: Initial state
    useSelector-->>Component: Render with data
    Note over Store: Action dispatched
    Store->>Reducer: Pass action
    Reducer->>Store: New state
    Store->>useSelector: State changed
    useSelector->>Component: Re-render with new data

data.title: Basic useSelector

data.text: There are several patterns for writing selectors. Each has trade-offs between simplicity, reusability, and performance.

rows: When you need full state access

data.text: For expensive computations, use `createSelector` from Redux Toolkit. Memoized selectors only recompute when their inputs change, preventing unnecessary re-renders.

data.title: Memoized Selectors

terms.definition: A function that extracts a specific piece of data from the Redux state.
Caching the result of a computation so it's only recalculated when inputs change.
A mechanism where components register to be notified when store state changes.

cards.title: useSelector (Hooks)
cards.content: Modern approach. Clean, functional syntax. Inline selector or custom hook. Part of react-redux v7+.

cards.title: connect (HOC)
cards.content: Legacy approach. Uses Higher-Order Component pattern. Verbose but explicit. Maintained for backward compatibility.

data.title: connect vs useSelector
Shallow Equality
data.text: useSelector uses strict equality (===) by default. If your selector returns an object or array, the component will re-render on every dispatch even if the values haven't changed. Return primitives or use shallowEqual.

items: Return primitive values (strings, numbers, booleans) when possible
Split selectors so each component only subscribes to what it needs
Use `useShallowSelector` or pass `shallowEqual` as second argument

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useSelector reads data from the Redux store and subscribes to updates
The selector function receives the entire state and returns the needed slice
Memoized selectors with createSelector prevent unnecessary computations
useSelector uses strict equality (===) - return primitives when possible
Modern hooks approach is cleaner than the legacy connect HOC
data.takeaway: useSelector is the primary hook for reading Redux state in React components, enabling efficient and reactive state access.
